references.text: The background to the conflict between Sarah and Hagar: Sarah gave her slave woman Hagar to Abraham, but when Hagar became pregnant, strife arose between them.
The immediate cause of Sarah's demand: Sarah saw that Hagar's son Ishmael was mocking (or playing with) Isaac.
God confirms Sarah's demand and tells Abraham to listen to her, for it is through Isaac his offspring shall be reckoned. The son of the slave woman will also become a nation.
Abraham gave all he had to Isaac, and sent away the sons of the concubines with gifts – fulfilling the principle Sarah expressed.
Paul quotes that it is through Isaac Abraham's offspring shall be reckoned, distinguishing between children of the flesh and children of the promise – directly linked to Sarah's words.
Paul uses the story of Sarah and Hagar as an allegory for the two covenants, quoting Sarah's words directly from Genesis 21:10 in verse 30.
Direct quotation and theological allegory: Paul uses the event to illustrate the distinction between children under the law and children under the promise.
Theological explanation: Romans 9:8 explains the principle of 'children of the promise' as the reason why Ishmael did not inherit with Isaac in Genesis 21.
